sanskrit: क्लैब्यं मा स्म गमः पार्थ नैतत्त्वय्युपपद्यते। क्षुद्रं हृदयदौर्बल्यं त्यक्त्वोत्तिष्ठ परन्तप॥
direct_translation: Do not yield to this faintheartedness, O Partha; it does not become you. Cast off this weakness of heart and arise.
meaning: Do not let fear, doubt, or discouragement keep you down. Get up and face what needs to be done.

sanskrit: मात्रास्पर्शास्तु कौन्तेय शीतोष्णसुखदुःखदाः। आगमापायिनोऽनित्यास्तांस्तितिक्षस्व भारत॥
direct_translation: Contact of the senses brings heat and cold, pleasure and pain. They come and go and are temporary; endure them, O Bharata.
meaning: Discomfort and bad moods do not last forever. Do not let temporary feelings stop your progress.

sanskrit: सुखदुःखे समे कृत्वा लाभालाभौ जयाजयौ। ततो युद्धाय युज्यस्व नैवं पापमवाप्स्यसि॥
direct_translation: Regarding pleasure and pain, gain and loss, victory and defeat alike, engage in your duty.
meaning: Show up with the same commitment whether things are going well or badly.

sanskrit: व्यवसायात्मिका बुद्धिरेकेह कुरुनन्दन। बहुशाखा ह्यनन्ताश्च बुद्धयोऽव्यवसायिनाम्॥
direct_translation: The understanding of the resolute is single-pointed, O joy of the Kurus; the thoughts of the irresolute branch endlessly.
meaning: A committed mind knows what matters and stays with it. A distracted mind keeps jumping between directions.

sanskrit: कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते मा फलेषु कदाचन। मा कर्मफलहेतुर्भूर्मा ते सङ्गोऽस्त्वकर्मणि॥
direct_translation: You have a claim to action alone, never to its fruits. Do not let the fruits of action be your motive, and do not become attached to inaction.
meaning: Focus on doing the work sincerely. You control your effort, not every result.

sanskrit: योगस्थः कुरु कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा धनञ्जय। सिद्ध्यसिद्ध्योः समो भूत्वा समत्वं योग उच्यते॥
direct_translation: Established in Yoga, perform your actions without attachment, O Dhananjaya. Remain even-minded in success and failure; such evenness is called Yoga.
meaning: Do your best without letting success excite you too much or failure make you quit.

sanskrit: बुद्धियुक्तो जहातीह उभे सुकृतदुष्कृते। तस्माद्योगाय युज्यस्व योगः कर्मसु कौशलम्॥
direct_translation: One endowed with steady understanding leaves behind both good and bad results. Therefore dedicate yourself to Yoga; Yoga is skillfulness in action.
meaning: Do not just work harder. Learn to work with attention, intelligence, and skill.

sanskrit: दुःखेष्वनुद्विग्नमनाः सुखेषु विगतस्पृहः। वीतरागभयक्रोधः स्थितधीर्मुनिरुच्यते॥
direct_translation: One whose mind remains undisturbed in sorrow, who does not crave pleasure, and who is free from attachment, fear, and anger is called one of steady wisdom.
meaning: Do not let difficult days break you or good days make you careless. Stay steady.

sanskrit: यदा संहरते चायं कूर्मोऽङ्गानीव सर्वशः। इन्द्रियाणीन्द्रियार्थेभ्यस्तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता॥
direct_translation: When one withdraws the senses from their objects on every side, as a tortoise withdraws its limbs, one's wisdom becomes firmly established.
meaning: Sometimes discipline means deliberately stepping away from distractions so you can protect your focus.

sanskrit: रागद्वेषवियुक्तैस्तु विषयानिन्द्रियैश्चरन्। आत्मवश्यैर्विधेयात्मा प्रसादमधिगच्छति॥
direct_translation: One who moves among sense objects with the senses under control, free from attraction and aversion, and with the self disciplined, attains serenity.
meaning: You do not need to remove every temptation. Learn to be around distractions without automatically obeying them.

sanskrit: नियतं कुरु कर्म त्वं कर्म ज्यायो ह्यकर्मणः। शरीरयात्रापि च ते न प्रसिद्ध्येदकर्मणः॥
direct_translation: Perform the action that is your duty, for action is superior to inaction. Even the maintenance of your body would not be possible through inaction.
meaning: Taking action is better than waiting for perfect motivation. Do the next thing that needs to be done.

sanskrit: तस्मादसक्तः सततं कार्यं कर्म समाचर। असक्तो ह्याचरन्कर्म परमाप्नोति पूरुषः॥
direct_translation: Therefore, without attachment, always perform the work that ought to be done; by performing action without attachment, a person reaches the highest.
meaning: Keep doing what needs to be done without constantly asking what reward you will get.

sanskrit: मयि सर्वाणि कर्माणि संन्यस्याध्यात्मचेतसा। निराशीर्निर्ममो भूत्वा युध्यस्व विगतज्वरः॥
direct_translation: Surrendering all actions to Me, with your mind centered in the Self, free from expectation and possessiveness, perform your duty without inner agitation.
meaning: Give yourself fully to your work without carrying unnecessary anxiety about the outcome.

sanskrit: श्रेयान्स्वधर्मो विगुणः परधर्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात्। स्वधर्मे निधनं श्रेयः परधर्मो भयावहः॥
direct_translation: Better is one's own duty, though imperfectly performed, than another's duty performed well. Better even to die in one's own duty; another's duty is dangerous.
meaning: Stay committed to the path that is truly yours instead of constantly comparing yourself with others.

sanskrit: एवं बुद्धेः परं बुद्ध्वा संस्तभ्यात्मानमात्मना। जहि शत्रुं महाबाहो कामरूपं दुरासदम्॥
direct_translation: Knowing the Self to be higher than the intellect, steady yourself through the Self and conquer the difficult enemy in the form of desire.
meaning: Do not let temporary cravings control your decisions. Use your better judgment to overcome impulses.

sanskrit: ब्रह्मण्याधाय कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा करोति यः। लिप्यते न स पापेन पद्मपत्रमिवाम्भसा॥
direct_translation: One who performs actions dedicating them to Brahman and abandoning attachment is not tainted by them, just as a lotus leaf is not wetted by water.
meaning: Work sincerely, but do not let ego, stress, or attachment consume you.

sanskrit: उद्धरेदात्मनात्मानं नात्मानमवसादयेत्। आत्मैव ह्यात्मनो बन्धुरात्मैव रिपुरात्मनः॥
direct_translation: Let a person lift themselves by themselves and not degrade themselves. The self alone is one's friend, and the self alone is one's enemy.
meaning: Your own habits can lift you or hold you back. Become someone who helps yourself move forward.

sanskrit: बन्धुरात्मात्मनस्तस्य येनात्मैवात्मना जितः। अनात्मनस्तु शत्रुत्वे वर्तेतात्मैव शत्रुवत्॥
direct_translation: For one who has conquered the self by the Self, the self is a friend; but for one who has not mastered the self, that very self behaves like an enemy.
meaning: Train your mind and it will support your goals. Leave it uncontrolled and it can sabotage them.

sanskrit: नात्यश्नतस्तु योगोऽस्ति न चैकान्तमनश्नतः। न चातिस्वप्नशीलस्य जाग्रतो नैव चार्जुन॥
direct_translation: Yoga is not for one who eats too much or too little, nor for one who sleeps too much or remains awake excessively, O Arjuna.
meaning: Discipline is not about extremes. Take care of basic things like food and sleep so you can stay consistent.

sanskrit: युक्ताहारविहारस्य युक्तचेष्टस्य कर्मसु। युक्तस्वप्नावबोधस्य योगो भवति दुःखहा॥
direct_translation: For one regulated in eating and recreation, balanced in effort and activity, and disciplined in sleep and waking, Yoga becomes the destroyer of sorrow.
meaning: Sustainable progress needs balance between work, rest, sleep, and recreation.

sanskrit: तं विद्याद्दुःखसंयोगवियोगं योगसंज्ञितम्। स निश्चयेन योक्तव्यो योगोऽनिर्विण्णचेतसा॥
direct_translation: Know that state called Yoga as separation from union with suffering. It should be practised with firm determination and without discouragement.
meaning: Keep practising with determination. Feeling discouraged is not a reason to stop.

sanskrit: शनैः शनैरुपरमेद् बुद्ध्या धृतिगृहीतया। आत्मसंस्थं मनः कृत्वा न किञ्चिदपि चिन्तयेत्॥
direct_translation: Gradually, little by little, one should become still through an intellect held firmly by patience, fixing the mind in the Self.
meaning: Improvement happens gradually. You do not need to change everything overnight—keep making small, steady progress.

sanskrit: यतो यतो निश्चरति मनश्चञ्चलमस्थिरम्। ततस्ततो नियम्यैतदात्मन्येव वशं नयेत्॥
direct_translation: Wherever the restless and unsteady mind wanders, from there one should restrain it and bring it back under control.
meaning: Getting distracted is normal. Discipline is noticing it and bringing your attention back again.

sanskrit: असंशयं महाबाहो मनो दुर्निग्रहं चलम्। अभ्यासेन तु कौन्तेय वैराग्येण च गृह्यते॥
direct_translation: Without doubt, O mighty-armed one, the mind is restless and difficult to control. But through practice and detachment it can be restrained.
meaning: Discipline is built through repeated practice. You do not need perfect control from the beginning.

sanskrit: असंयतात्मना योगो दुष्प्राप इति मे मतिः। वश्यात्मना तु यतता शक्योऽवाप्तुमुपायतः॥
direct_translation: For one whose mind is uncontrolled, Yoga is difficult to attain. But it can be attained by one who has mastered the mind and strives through the proper means.
meaning: Self-control is difficult, but it can be developed through the right method and persistent effort.

sanskrit: प्रयत्नाद्यतमानस्तु योगी संशुद्धकिल्बिषः। अनेकजन्मसंसिद्धस्ततो याति परां गतिम्॥
direct_translation: The yogi who strives with sustained effort, becoming purified and perfected over many births, eventually reaches the highest goal.
meaning: Deep improvement takes time. Keep putting in sincere effort even when progress feels slow.

sanskrit: यत्करोषि यदश्नासि यज्जुहोषि ददासि यत्। यत्तपस्यसि कौन्तेय तत्कुरुष्व मदर्पणम्॥
direct_translation: Whatever you do, whatever you eat, whatever you offer or give, and whatever austerity you undertake, O Kaunteya, do that as an offering to Me.
meaning: Give even ordinary daily actions a higher purpose. Dedication can turn small tasks into meaningful work.

sanskrit: सन्तुष्टः सततं योगी यतात्मा दृढनिश्चयः। मय्यर्पितमनोबुद्धिर्यो मद्भक्तः स मे प्रियः॥
direct_translation: One who is always content, steadfast in Yoga, self-controlled, firmly resolved, and whose mind and intellect are dedicated to Me—that devotee is dear to Me.
meaning: Be steady, self-controlled, and firmly committed instead of depending on constant motivation.

sanskrit: समः शत्रौ च मित्रे च तथा मानापमानयोः। शीतोष्णसुखदुःखेषु समः सङ्गविवर्जितः॥
direct_translation: Equal toward friend and foe, in honor and dishonor, in heat and cold, pleasure and pain, and free from attachment.
meaning: Do not let praise, criticism, comfort, or difficulty determine how seriously you pursue your work.

sanskrit: नियतं सङ्गरहितमरागद्वेषतः कृतम्। अफलप्रेप्सुना कर्म यत्तत्सात्त्विकमुच्यते॥
direct_translation: Action that is one's duty, performed without attachment, without attraction or aversion, and without seeking its fruit, is called Sattvic.
meaning: Do the work because it needs to be done, not only because an immediate reward is waiting.

sanskrit: मुक्तसङ्गोऽनहंवादी धृत्युत्साहसमन्वितः। सिद्ध्यसिद्ध्योर्निर्विकारः कर्ता सात्त्विक उच्यते॥
direct_translation: A doer who is free from attachment and ego, endowed with firmness and enthusiasm, and unchanged by success or failure is called Sattvic.
meaning: Work with both determination and enthusiasm without letting success or failure change your commitment.

sanskrit: धृत्या यया धारयते मनःप्राणेन्द्रियक्रियाः। योगेनाव्यभिचारिण्या धृतिः सा पार्थ सात्त्विकी॥
direct_translation: The firmness by which one unwaveringly holds the activities of the mind, vital force, and senses through Yoga is called Sattvic firmness.
meaning: Real determination means staying committed even after the excitement and motivation fade.

sanskrit: सुखं त्विदानीं त्रिविधं शृणु मे भरतर्षभ। अभ्यासाद्रमते यत्र दुःखान्तं च निगच्छति॥
direct_translation: Now hear from Me of the three kinds of happiness, O best of the Bharatas: that in which one comes to delight through practice and reaches the end of suffering.
meaning: Something difficult can become enjoyable when you practise it consistently.

sanskrit: यत्तदग्रे विषमिव परिणामेऽमृतोपमम्। तत्सुखं सात्त्विकं प्रोक्तमात्मबुद्धिप्रसादजम्॥
direct_translation: That which is like poison in the beginning but like nectar in the end, arising from clarity of understanding, is said to be Sattvic happiness.
meaning: The right habits often feel difficult at first but become deeply rewarding with time.

sanskrit: स्वे स्वे कर्मण्यभिरतः संसिद्धिं लभते नरः। स्वकर्मनिरतः सिद्धिं यथा विन्दति तच्छृणु॥
direct_translation: A person devoted to their own work attains perfection. Hear how one devoted to one's own duty attains success.
meaning: Mastery comes from staying dedicated to meaningful work long enough to become excellent at it.

sanskrit: श्रेयान्स्वधर्मो विगुणः परधर्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात्। स्वभावनियतं कर्म कुर्वन्नाप्नोति किल्बिषम्॥
direct_translation: One's own duty, though imperfectly performed, is better than another's duty performed well. Performing the work determined by one's own nature, one does not incur fault.
meaning: You do not need to be perfect. Keep improving at the work and responsibilities that are genuinely yours.
